title: Export PDUs to Files: Don't error out on anonymous dissectors
description:
Call dissector_handle_get_short_name() instead of
dissector_handle_get_dissector_name() when passing information about
dissector handles to export PDUs, which expects protocol names instead
of dissector names anyway. A lot of heuristic dissectors set dissector
handles in conversations with anonymous handles, which then caused things
to break because NULL names for the protocols weren't handled.

Closes #16884

notes.body:
IMHO this is not the right way to fix things. As explained in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/exported_pdu.h#L78, the EXP_PDU_TAG_PROTO_NAME tag is used for the registered protocol name. By always taking the short protocol name, you take the risk of breaking this assumption and preventing the decoding of protocols registered by name if it is different.

You should at a minimum use the registered dissector name if it exists to ensure that you do not break things. If it does not exist, and if we still want to decode the payload (as this is the purpose of the export PDU functionality) then we should probably add a new tag saying that we should perform the lookup on another criteria (here the TCP port for example). But handling all cases might be challenging and IMHO dissectors should have been registered by name in the first place.
Shold we instead write out a warning/pop up an error and refuse the export?

Ah, I see, yes, since, as your comment says, it uses the name to call the dissector then using the protocol short name won't work since that isn't always the same. I was confused because the field and constant name uses ```PROTO_NAME``` when it's really the dissector name (which makes sense, might want to hand it off to different specific dissectors.)

So the proper fix is to go through every dissector and replace all the calls to ```create_dissector_handle``` with either ```create_dissector_handle_with_name``` or ```register_dissector``` (_preferred_ - *because unless it's registered the dissector won't actually get called when exported*) so that they have names? Anonymous dissectors should be generally deprecated?

And on the TCP, UDP, etc. side if anonymous dissector registration isn't removed then the suggestion to check for a NULL value and write out a more informative warning makes sense.

I guess anonymous dissectors still work for dissectors that are called only based on entries in dissector tables, if I understand the code and how it handles EXP_PDU_TAG_DISSECTOR_TABLE_NAME and EXP_PDU_TAG_DISSECTOR_TABLE_NAME_NUM_VAL.

I wonder if it would be possible to indicate the TCP port table in case of
no proto name for TCP based communicationm similar for UDP.
We already do this for port based dissection (see handle_export_pdu_dissection_table() in packet-tcp.c). But it won't be used if the dissector is set via the conversation for example.
